title: Innate Colour Preference in Zebrafish (Danio rerio)
author: Hagen, Zhang, et al.

steps.title: Transfer fish to testing room
steps.instruction: Remove fish from the main housing system, place 10‑15 fish per smaller tank, and transport the tanks to the testing room; allow a 20‑minute acclimation period and keep all tanks, beakers, and the plus‑maze on heat mats to maintain water temperature.

steps.title: Fill maze with water
steps.instruction: Fill the plus‑maze arena to a depth of 5 cm using habitat water.

steps.title: Insert coloured sheets
steps.instruction: Place plastic coloured sheets (red, yellow, blue, green) at the ends of each arm, fully submerged in the water to avoid differences in reflectivity.

steps.title: Set up tracking system
steps.instruction: Open EthoVision (or equivalent) and select the differencing detection method; ensure the arena is visually isolated with white corrugated plastic shielding; measure room luminance (~32 cd/m³) with a CalSpot photometer and calibrate if needed.

steps.title: Introduce fish to centre
steps.instruction: Gently place a single fish into the neutral centre zone of the plus maze.

steps.title: Record behaviour
steps.instruction: Track the fish for a continuous 10‑minute trial using the motion‑tracking software.

steps.title: Sex fish after trial
steps.instruction: Transfer the fish to a small beaker containing habitat water; allow ~10 minutes for colour recovery; determine sex by anal‑fin colour (yellow = male, clear = female) and body shape (slender male vs. rounded female); then move the fish to a separate tank with other tested fish.

steps.title: Refresh water and rotate colours
steps.instruction: Replace arena water minimally every 3‑5 fish and randomly rotate the four colour sheets between trials to prevent directional bias; using the same water for up to 5 fish does not affect behaviour; monitor and maintain water temperature between trials if water is not changed.

steps.title: Analyze zone occupancy
steps.instruction: Export tracking data and quantify time spent in each coloured zone; test for normality with the D’Agostino & Pearson test; if data are normal, perform a one‑way ANOVA, otherwise use a Kruskal‑Wallis test; follow with the appropriate post‑hoc comparison.

steps.title: Maintain feeding schedule
steps.instruction: Do not feed fish before behavioural testing, as feeding can alter responses; feed only after all trials are completed.
